sections.title: Design Skills
sections.blurb: The default output looks like every other AI-generated page: same fonts, same purple gradient, same card layout. These make Claude pick a direction first.

sections.title: Site-Wide Theming & Design Tokens
sections.blurb: Design skills teach Claude to think about aesthetics. These produce the config: CSS variables, Tailwind @theme blocks, dark-mode tokens, so the whole site stays consistent without re-explaining the brand.

sections.title: Animation & Motion
sections.blurb: Library knowledge for actually implementing motion: GSAP timelines, Motion variants, scroll-triggered effects, and motion audits.

sections.title: UI/UX Intelligence
sections.blurb: Design thinking, UX research, growth and accessibility patterns.

sections.title: Design-to-Code Pipeline
sections.blurb: Figma to tokens to components to code, and back.

sections.title: Testing & Browser Automation
sections.blurb: Claude cannot see the UI by default. These give it a browser, DevTools and a component library to check against.

sections.title: Docs & Context
sections.blurb: Training data is stale. These fetch current, version-specific documentation.

sections.title: Framework Skills
sections.blurb: Specialised knowledge for specific frontend tech, plus the polish pipeline.

sections.title: Deploy & Preview
sections.blurb: Preview deployments and zero-config hosting from inside the session.

tools.name: Frontend Design (Official)
tools.author: Anthropic
tools.summary: Anthropic's own skill: Claude picks an actual aesthetic direction before writing code instead of defaulting to Inter, a purple gradient and rounded cards. Install this first; everything else assumes it.
tools.notes: Requires real typography pairing, blocks generic component patterns and cookie-cutter layouts, enforces CSS variables and cohesive color systems. Lives in the built-in claude-plugins-official marketplace, so no marketplace add is needed.

tools.name: UI/UX Pro Max
tools.author: nextlevelbuilder
tools.summary: 240+ styles, 127 font pairings, 99 UX guidelines. Say "fintech dashboard" and it picks a design system that fits fintech; the v2 reasoning engine does the style matching.
tools.notes: Also installable through its CLI: `npm install -g ui-ux-pro-max-cli && uipro init --ai claude`. An older CLI package with a similar name is stale; use only ui-ux-pro-max-cli. Works with Cursor, Windsurf, Codex and a dozen other agents.

tools.name: Taste Skill
tools.author: Leonxlnx
tools.summary: Tunable knobs for how wild Claude gets: design variance (safe to experimental), motion intensity (subtle to cinematic), visual density (spacious to compact).
requires: a Chromium browser for the default skill
tools.notes: Bundles several skills: design-taste-frontend (default), redesign-existing-projects, image-to-code, high-end-visual-design, minimalist-ui, industrial-brutalist-ui, brandkit. Alternative: `npx skills add https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill`.

tools.name: Frontend Design Pro Demo
tools.author: ClaudeKit
tools.summary: Eleven named aesthetics (Swiss Minimalism, Glassmorphism, Brutalism, Dark OLED Luxury, Organic Biomorphic, …) with working HTML/CSS demos and the master prompts that generated them. Say "use the Dark OLED Luxury style" and Claude knows what you mean.
tools.notes: Last updated late 2025; the demos remain a useful vocabulary even if the skill itself is not maintained.

tools.name: Bencium UX Designer
tools.author: bencium
tools.summary: Two modes: Controlled (ship to prod: WCAG, full responsive specs, motion constraints) and Innovative (explore: bold, break rules). Ships ~830 lines of accessibility guidance and ~600 lines of responsive patterns as reference files Claude loads when needed.
tools.notes: The marketplace is named bencium-marketplace and also carries bencium-innovative-ux-designer, design-audit and typography. Files: SKILL.md, ACCESSIBILITY.md, RESPONSIVE-DESIGN.md, MOTION-SPEC.md, DESIGN-SYSTEM-TEMPLATE.md.

tools.name: Brand Guidelines Skill
tools.author: Anthropic
tools.summary: Anthropic's own brand colors and typography as a skill. Not useful on its own, but a clean template for a brand skill for your company.
tools.notes: Copy the structure: a SKILL.md with the palette, type scale and voice rules, plus reference files for logos and assets.

tools.name: Design System Architect
tools.author: community
tools.summary: Builds a full token system from scratch: OKLCH color space (P3 wide gamut), 4px spacing grid, semantic light/dark theming, typography scale. Outputs a Tailwind v4 @theme block.
tools.notes: Manual install: copy the skill folder into ~/.claude/skills/. Generates semantic color mapping, brand-tinted neutrals, typography scale, spacing grid and dark-mode tokens that become Tailwind utilities automatically.

tools.name: Design Tokens Skill
tools.author: phrazzld
tools.summary: Builds the entire color system off a single --brand-hue variable in OKLCH. Change one number and everything re-themes: primary, backgrounds, borders, muted states.
tools.notes: The site-theming skill in this plugin reproduces the approach so it works without installing anything.

tools.name: Tailwind CSS Kit
tools.author: blencorp
tools.summary: Auto-activating Tailwind v4 skill: CSS-first @theme (no tailwind.config.js), dark-mode patterns, responsive utilities, component extraction, plugin setup (forms, typography).
tools.notes: Part of blencorp/claude-code-kit; install through that kit's CLI or copy the skill folder.

tools.name: UI Styling Skill (ClaudeKit)
tools.author: ClaudeKit
tools.summary: shadcn/ui + Tailwind + form handling in one skill: themed component configs, @layer organisation, dark-mode toggle, react-hook-form + zod patterns. The pick if your stack is shadcn.
tools.notes: Manual copy into ~/.claude/skills/.

tools.name: Tailwind Styling Skill (MajesticLabs)
tools.author: majesticlabs-dev
tools.summary: React-focused Tailwind styling: component-level theming, responsive layouts, design-system integration. Lighter than the ClaudeKit version if you do not need shadcn.
tools.notes: Manual copy into ~/.claude/skills/.

tools.name: Create Design System Rules (Figma)
tools.author: community
tools.summary: Point it at your Figma file and it generates a rules file Claude follows on every task: where components live, which tokens to use, spacing scale, Tailwind conventions. Set-and-forget consistency.
tools.notes: Output includes component directory rules, token enforcement (never hardcode hex), spacing scale and Figma-to-code workflow steps.

tools.name: CLAUDE.md Theme Block
tools.author: Anthropic (Frontend Aesthetics Cookbook)
tools.summary: Not a plugin: five lines in CLAUDE.md that lock a site-wide aesthetic. The fastest way to enforce a direction. No install.
tools.notes: This plugin writes the block for you with /frontend-design-toolkit:theme. Presets: Cyberpunk, Editorial, SaaS Minimal, Dark OLED Luxury, Brutalist, Retro-Futuristic, Organic, Art Deco, Solarpunk.

tools.name: Animation Design Skills (freshtechbro)
tools.author: freshtechbro
tools.summary: 22 skills plus 5 bundles covering the animation and 3D libraries: GSAP + ScrollTrigger, Motion, React Spring, Lottie, anime.js, Locomotive Scroll, Barba.js, Three.js, React Three Fiber, Babylon.js, A-Frame, PixiJS. Each auto-activates for its library.
tools.notes: Install individual plugins by name (gsap-scrolltrigger, motion-framer, react-three-fiber, …) or bundles (core-3d-animation, extended-3d-scroll, animation-components, authoring-motion). Last pushed late 2025.

tools.name: Motion Skill (jezweb)
tools.author: jezweb
tools.summary: Focused on Motion (formerly Framer Motion): declarative animations, gestures, scroll effects, spring physics, layout animations, SVG. Includes bundle patterns (LazyMotion at 4.6 KB, useAnimate at 2.3 KB). Tested against React 19, Next.js 16, Vite 7, Tailwind v4.
tools.notes: Manual copy into ~/.claude/skills/.

tools.name: Design Motion Principles
tools.author: kylezantos
tools.summary: Motion audit skill trained on Emil Kowalski, Jakub Krehel and Jhey Tompkins. Finds conditional UI that should animate but does not (renders without AnimatePresence, dynamic styles without transitions) and gives per-designer recommendations by severity.
tools.notes: Not a plugin (no marketplace manifest); install as a skill. Good for reviewing existing code, not only generating animations.

tools.name: Wondelai UX/Growth Skills
tools.author: wondelai
tools.summary: Skills based on actual books (Don Norman, Cialdini, Ries, Hormozi): UX design, marketing and CRO, product strategy, growth.
tools.notes: Other plugins in the marketplace: marketing-cro, product-strategy, product-innovation, strategy-growth.

tools.name: Google Stitch Skills
tools.author: Google Labs
tools.summary: Google Labs' design skills: design-md (manage DESIGN.md), enhance-prompt (design vocabulary), react-components and shadcn-ui (Stitch to code), stitch-loop (iterative design-code loop), remotion (walkthrough videos).
tools.notes: Three groups: stitch-design, stitch-build, stitch-utilities. The Stitch MCP server itself needs a Google API key; follow Google's setup page for the current endpoint.

tools.name: Jeffallan Claude Skills
tools.author: Jeffallan
tools.summary: 66-skill full-stack library. Frontend-relevant: React Expert (Server Components, hooks), Vue Expert, Angular Expert, Tailwind CSS Expert, CSS/SCSS Expert, Accessibility Specialist, Responsive Design Specialist.
tools.notes: One large plugin; check its token footprint with `claude plugin details` before enabling it everywhere.

tools.name: UI/UX Design Skill (Useforclaude)
tools.author: Useforclaude
tools.summary: Kitchen sink of UX knowledge: research, personas, flows, wireframing, usability testing, information architecture, Gestalt, Fitts's and Hick's laws, WCAG, mobile-first.
tools.notes: Manual copy into ~/.claude/skills/.

tools.name: Figma MCP Server (Official)
tools.author: Figma
tools.summary: Claude reads Figma files directly: frames, components, tokens, layout. Works in reverse too: "Send this to Figma" captures running UI as editable layers (Code to Canvas).
requires: Figma account (Dev or Full seat for Dev Mode features)
Figma desktop app for the local server
tools.notes: Remote alternative: `claude mcp add --transport http figma https://mcp.figma.com/mcp` then /mcp to authenticate. Desktop server: `claude mcp add --transport http figma-desktop http://127.0.0.1:3845/mcp` (the old /sse endpoint is deprecated). Key tools: get_design_context, get_variable_defs, get_code_connect_map, generate_figma_design. Costs 3 to 4k tokens at session start.

tools.name: Figma Code Connect
tools.author: Figma
tools.summary: A Figma feature, not an MCP: maps Figma components to your real code components, so get_code_connect_map makes Claude reuse your <Button> instead of inventing one. Kills duplicate components.
tools.notes: Configured on the Figma side plus *.figma.tsx files in the repo.

tools.name: Web Artifacts Builder
tools.author: community (awesome-claude-skills)
tools.summary: For multi-component claude.ai HTML artifacts with React, Tailwind and shadcn/ui: component composition, proper Tailwind usage, modern React patterns.
tools.notes: Listed in the ComposioHQ awesome-claude-skills directory.

tools.name: Playwright MCP
tools.author: Microsoft
tools.summary: The standard browser for Claude: 25+ tools driven by accessibility-tree snapshots (2 to 5 KB) instead of screenshots (500 KB+). Navigate, click, fill forms, screenshot, read the rendered DOM.
install: claude mcp add playwright -s user -- npx @playwright/mcp@latest
tools.notes: Flags worth knowing: --vision auto (switches to vision for canvas/WebGL), --save-video=800x600, --caps=devtools for Core Web Vitals, Chrome extension bridge to reuse a logged-in browser. Also `claude plugin install playwright@claude-plugins-official`. Costs ~5.3k tokens at session start; see playwright-cli for the cheaper option.

tools.name: Playwright CLI + Skills
tools.author: Microsoft
tools.summary: Microsoft's companion CLI, now recommended over the MCP for coding agents: the same browser control from Bash with roughly a quarter of the tokens (27k vs 114k on the same task).
tools.notes: `playwright-cli install --skills` drops the skills into ~/.claude/skills so Claude knows the commands. Prefer this when the context budget is tight.

tools.name: Chrome DevTools MCP
tools.author: Google (ChromeDevTools)
tools.summary: When Playwright is not enough: console inspection, network analysis, performance profiling, DOM exploration, HAR export, device emulation. The Network and Performance tabs, readable by Claude.
install: claude mcp add chrome-devtools --scope user -- npx chrome-devtools-mcp@latest
tools.notes: Published by Google, not Anthropic; the package is chrome-devtools-mcp. Also `claude plugin install chrome-devtools-mcp@claude-plugins-official`. Costs 5 to 6k tokens at session start; enable it for profiling sessions, not permanently.

tools.name: Webapp Testing Skill
tools.author: lackeyjb
tools.summary: Model-invoked Playwright automation: auto-activates when Claude detects it needs to test something in a browser.
tools.notes: Listed in the ComposioHQ awesome-claude-skills directory.

tools.name: Storybook MCP
tools.author: Storybook / Chromatic
tools.summary: Gives Claude your Storybook: look up existing components, read docs and stories, get build instructions before generating new UI. Stops Claude reinventing components you already have. Visual regression through Chromatic on every PR.
install: claude mcp add --transport http --scope project storybook http://localhost:6006/mcp
tools.notes: For a Chromatic-hosted Storybook, point the URL at the hosted /mcp endpoint instead of localhost.

tools.name: Visual Regression Skill
tools.author: alekspetrov
tools.summary: Generates Storybook stories, Chromatic/Percy/BackstopJS config and CI workflows for visual regression. Say "set up visual regression for my Button" and it detects the stack, writes stories for every variant and wires the pipeline.
tools.notes: Part of the alekspetrov/navigator marketplace.

tools.name: Web Quality Skills (Addy Osmani)
tools.author: addyosmani
tools.summary: From Google's web performance lead: skills for Core Web Vitals (LCP, INP, CLS), accessibility (WCAG 2.1), SEO and best practices, plus an orchestrator that runs a full-site audit. Framework-aware for Next.js, Vue/Nuxt, Svelte and plain HTML.
tools.notes: Alternative: `npx skills add addyosmani/web-quality-skills` (the older add-skill package is deprecated). Skills: web-quality-audit, performance, core-web-vitals, accessibility, seo, best-practices.

tools.name: Context7
tools.author: Upstash
tools.summary: Live, version-specific docs for whatever framework you use. On React 19 it pulls React 19 docs, not React 18 from training data. 1000+ libraries. Matters most for React 19 vs 18, Tailwind v4 vs v3, Next.js App Router vs Pages.
install: claude mcp add --scope user context7 -- npx -y @upstash/context7-mcp@latest
tools.notes: Works anonymously with lower rate limits; add `--api-key YOUR_KEY` after the package name for higher ones. Remote option: `claude mcp add --scope user --transport http context7 https://mcp.context7.com/mcp`. Also `claude plugin install context7@claude-plugins-official`. Only ~2k tokens idle because docs are fetched on demand.

tools.name: Skill Seekers
tools.author: yusufkaraaslan
tools.summary: Point it at any docs site and it generates a Claude skill from the content. For internal component libraries or frameworks Context7 does not cover.
tools.notes: A Python tool, not a plugin; the generated skill folder is what you install.

tools.name: Firecrawl MCP
tools.author: Firecrawl
tools.summary: Web scraping as an MCP server: scrape docs, competitor sites, design inspiration. Fills gaps when Context7 lacks what you need.
install: claude mcp add --transport http firecrawl https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp
tools.notes: Keyless endpoint has low limits; add `--header "Authorization: Bearer fc-…"` with an API key for real use. Local alternative: `claude mcp add firecrawl -e FIRECRAWL_API_KEY=fc-… -- npx -y firecrawl-mcp`. Also `claude plugin install firecrawl@claude-plugins-official`.

tools.name: D3.js Visualization
tools.author: chrisvoncsefalvay
tools.summary: Teaches Claude to produce D3 charts and interactive data visualisations.
tools.notes: Listed in the ComposioHQ awesome-claude-skills directory.

tools.name: Three.js Skills
tools.author: CloudAI-X
tools.summary: Ten skills from fundamentals to interaction for 3D elements and interactive experiences with Three.js.
tools.notes: Not a plugin: clone and copy the .claude/skills folders into your project or ~/.claude/skills/.

tools.name: shadcn/ui Skill (Google Stitch)
tools.author: Google Labs
tools.summary: Build UI components with shadcn/ui, part of the Stitch skills (stitch-build group).
tools.notes: Installed together with the rest of stitch-skills.

tools.name: TypeScript LSP
tools.author: Anthropic
tools.summary: Real-time type checking through the Language Server Protocol: errors surface before Claude finishes writing. If you write TypeScript, install it.
tools.notes: Near-zero context cost: diagnostics arrive as tool feedback, not schemas.

tools.name: Baseline UI (ui-skills)
tools.author: ibelick (ui-skills.com)
tools.summary: Step 2 of the polish pipeline: fixes spacing, typography, alignment and interactive states on a generated page.
tools.notes: The ui-skills CLI subcommands are start, categories, list, get; there is no `add`. Also available as an MCP endpoint at https://www.ui-skills.com/mcp.

tools.name: Fixing Accessibility (ui-skills)
tools.author: ibelick (ui-skills.com)
tools.summary: Step 3 of the polish pipeline: keyboard, labels, focus, semantics.
tools.notes: Run after baseline-ui, before fixing-motion-performance.

tools.name: Fixing Motion & Performance (ui-skills)
tools.author: ibelick (ui-skills.com)
tools.summary: Step 4 of the polish pipeline: reduced-motion support, animation performance, perf budgets.
tools.notes: Design, then craft, then a11y, then perf. That is the loop; the ui-polish-loop skill in this plugin runs it by hand when these are not installed.

tools.name: Vercel MCP
tools.author: Vercel
tools.summary: Deployments, builds, logs, domains and env vars from inside the session. Deploy preview branches and check build status without leaving Claude Code.
install: claude mcp add --transport http vercel https://mcp.vercel.com
tools.notes: Also `claude plugin install vercel@claude-plugins-official`. Scope it to the project unless every repo deploys to Vercel.

tools.name: PinMe
tools.author: glitternetwork
tools.summary: Zero-config deploy: no servers, no accounts. Point it at a directory, get a URL.
tools.notes: A skill wrapper is available with `npx skills add glitternetwork/pinme`.
